newsitem.title: GERMANY: Suspect arrives in Germany to face bomb probe.
newsitem.headline: Suspect arrives in Germany to face bomb probe.

text.p: A German woman wanted in connection with a fatal 1986 West Berlin nightclub bombing which led to a U.S. air strike on Libya arrived back in Germany on Wednesday after being extradited from Greece.
The suspect, Andrea Hausler, 31, was arrested last October in Halkidiki near Salonika at the request of German authorities who want to put her on trial.
The bomb attack in Berlin's Schoeneberg district killed two U.S. soldiers and a Turkish woman and wounded scores of off-duty U.S. military personnel.
Washington blamed Libya for the blast and bombed the Arab state, killing at least 15 people and wounding more than 100.

Hausler was arrested while on holiday with her two-year-old son and boyfriend. A spokesman for German border police said she had arrived in Munich on board a Lufthansa plane and would be taken on to Berlin.
Two other people were arrested in Germany in October in connection with the bombing.
